title: The target reach is the whole map: delete P.maxTargetDist's cap (56 since E0300) and gatherCandidates' diamond branch
hypothesis: General quantity: the path length at which a target stops being worth walking to, against the map's torus diameter (W+H)/2. E0300 kept maxTargetDist = 56 (+16.4 Elo, 498 pairs, H1), a swept constant chosen as one of 120 variants. On the official, retired, community and Sprint maps the torus diameter is at most 56 on every map but the two 64x64 ones (64), so 56 already works as 'no cap': it binds only on 64x64 boards and where kelp makes the path longer than 56. gatherCandidates' diamond branch (2*radius+1 < W or H) no longer runs on any map up to 112 wide, so every turn already scans every tile (CPU p50 4.2M -> 5.3M, p99 13.1M, max 17.9M in E0300's gate, 13 games). Change, like for like: a candidate's reach is the whole reachable map (the BFS bound becomes the map, as headField already is). A fast tile's or a drop's yield still divides its cost, so the order of candidates is unchanged; P.maxTargetDist, the diamond branch and the reach field go. params.hpp's comment ('ignore pearls further than this') also becomes wrong in kind: the cap bounds every target kind, and spawn tiles were 52% of the moves E0300's shadow count changed (7,702 of 14,718, 114 games), so the comments that remain say 'targets'. Options: (1) delete the cap (this idea): no constant left, one branch less; (2) I466: reach from the dragon's own pearl rate while exploring, which this idea is the limit of (a very large reach factor); if I466 is kept first, this idea is moot; (3) reach = the torus diameter x yield, a map-size formula that plays exactly as (1) except around kelp detours; (1) is chosen because it deletes the most and (3) differs from it on few moves. Measure first: a logging copy of the champion that computes the uncapped target beside its own (as E0300's shadow copy did for 14 v 56) on fresh eval maps, fresh worldgen maps and renamed copies of maps/ladder, maps/sprint and maps/retired, counted apart; stop only if changed moves are under 0.1 a game on both our generator's maps and off-generator maps by the rate rule. Scenarios: a 64x64 board with one pearl 60 steps away round a kelp wall and nothing nearer: the dragon targets it (today it explores); boundary: a 32x32 board plays identically. E0300's per-opponent split (champion 0.584 v swarm 0.491 over 83 trials each, z 2.61) did not reproduce: on 24 fresh maps both sides against the swarm the kept 56 won 45 of 48 to the old 14's 40 of 48 (better on 6 map-sides, worse on 1, sign p 0.06), so no opponent condition is proposed. The judge flagged worldgen: 0.507 over 187 trials against 0.534 over 311 on our generator's maps (z 1.61, suggestive, n = 498): read this idea's worldgen line apart.
